Percentage letter/word spacing: fixes and performance
Recorded 2026-11-02

Fixed 16 selected CSS syntax assertions across four files, with no new mismatch
keys. Before: 16,451 / 18,469 pass (89.07%); after: 16,467 / 18,469 (89.16%).
The same selection and 13,434 unrepresented assertions remain.

Implementation

Lightning CSS remains unchanged and the sole CSS parser. Its shared native
LengthPercentage parser accepts percentage values that its property-specific
Spacing representation cannot store. The existing native math-type guard is
reused before the text handler applies the existing TextSpacing conversion.
Standalone percentage tokens are converted directly from the native token AST,
avoiding printing/reparsing. Mixed expressions still use the native value parser.

Examples include letter-spacing:120%, word-spacing:-10%, and mixed expressions
such as calc(2ch - 30%). Negative spacing remains valid. Absolute lengths and
percentage coefficients remain separate in the existing model, preserving
percentage inheritance relative to the recipient used font size. Existing normal/
length declarations retain their path. No renderer or GPUI change is needed.

The existing converter does not represent mixed non-linear percentage math.
Those expressions keep its current rejection behavior; this change does not
claim every CSS Text math expression is rendered. Font-metric-dependent lengths
also retain existing resolution requirements. Sources:
https://drafts.csswg.org/css-text-4/#letter-spacing-property
https://drafts.csswg.org/css-text-4/#word-spacing-property

Validation

305 existing style tests, 32 declaration-validation tests and five reader font-
scaling tests pass (342 total). Offline cargo check passes. The full pinned audit
scanned 35,417 files / 32,021 literal calls, with zero dependency parser panics
and no new mismatch keys. Its diagnostic exit 101 is expected while 2,002
mismatches remain. Computed helpers check syntax only, not computed output.
No image suite was rerun. Existing test/benchmark sources and all expectation/
selection ledgers are unchanged.

Performance

The baseline is the preceding selector-cache stage. Existing benchmark sources
were compiled unchanged with identical frozen native/support dependencies,
rustc opt-level=2 and debuginfo=0. Ten cases, 15 alternating before/after pairs
each: 300 final process runs, pinned CPU 6. Another 300 initial implementation
runs are retained. Host load/frequency/boost are uncontrolled.
Positive means slower. Diagnostic 95% bootstrap intervals use 5,000 resamples of
paired median percentage changes, without multiple-comparison adjustment.
Intervals containing zero are inconclusive. EPUB totals sum five fixture medians,
not a single page. Cold means uncached author programs with machine/default-CSS
caches warmed.

Workload                         Paired change    95% bootstrap range    Assessment
cascade-plain                      +6.09%    [  +5.04%,   +6.37%]   slowdown
cascade-vars-inline                -0.09%    [  -2.52%,   +1.26%]   inconclusive
epub-cold                          +0.61%    [  -0.95%,   +1.38%]   inconclusive
epub-cached                        -0.29%    [  -0.99%,   +0.51%]   inconclusive
spacing-equivalent-cold           +29.56%    [ +28.74%,  +30.50%]   slowdown
spacing-equivalent-cached         +31.83%    [ +31.00%,  +32.54%]   slowdown
spacing-feature-cold              +25.37%    [ +24.85%,  +25.56%]   slowdown
spacing-feature-cached            +26.38%    [ +25.08%,  +27.90%]   slowdown
normalization                      +0.73%    [  -1.39%,   +2.38%]   inconclusive
normalization-retry                -1.50%    [  -2.29%,   +0.32%]   inconclusive

Both spacing workloads add feature work: the baseline ignores the new percentage
declarations and the changed build applies them. With 64 classes at 16px, the
first uses 0% and calc(2px - 6.25%) after literal 0px/1px fallbacks, designed to
retain the same used spacing. Pixel equality was not checked. The second uses
2% and calc(2px + 5%), intentionally producing different spacing. Neither is a
comparison of equivalent parsing/conversion work.

The first implementation reparsed every percentage, measuring about 31-37%
extra style time on the feature workloads. Standalone native percentage tokens
now avoid that round trip. The 300 initial runs, original source hashes and all
initial metrics remain in the performance artifacts alongside final results.
Mixed-expression serialization/reparsing still adds allocations. All
positive, negative and inconclusive timings, allocations and peak-byte counts
are retained in spacing-fix-performance.json, with raw stdout and binary hashes
in spacing-fix-performance-runs.jsonl.gz. No unconditional speed claim is made.

Registry

2,002 mismatches remain: 178 confirmed dependency blocks and 1,824 unresolved.
All 2,236 original observations are retained, including 234 now fixed across
the syntax-fix stages. Original actual/native observations retain snapshot meaning.
Earlier selector and local-fix reports remain historical evidence. Exact new
fixed keys are in spacing-fix-results.jsonl; current mismatches are in
spacing-fix-after-mismatches.jsonl. All build outputs and compiler scratch use
disk-backed storage. Full baseline, audit/build logs and binaries: /home/johan/.cache/html-wpt-spacing-fixes
